276:## The `answer( )` elaborator
277-
278-Some open questions are formulated in a way that requires a user-provided
279-answer, for instance the
280-[Hadwiger–Nelson problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hadwiger%E2%80%93Nelson_problem)
281-asks for the minimum number of colours needed to colour the plane such that
282-no two points exactly one unit distance apart have the same colour. The
283:`answer( )` elaborator allows us to formulate the problem without deciding
284-for an answer.
285-
286-```lean
287-@[category research open]
288-theorem HadwigerNelsonProblem :
289:    UnitDistancePlaneGraph.chromaticNumber = answer(sorry) := by
290-  sorry
291-```
292-
293-### Problems that require answers
294-
295:Note that providing a term inside the `answer( )` elaborator together with a
296-proof that the statement is true *does not* by itself mean that the problem
297-has been solved. For example, a question of the form "Which natural numbers
298-satisfy the predicate $P$?" might be formalised as
299-
300-```lean
301:theorem myOpenProblem : {n : ℕ | P n} = answer(sorry) := by
302-  sorry
303-```
304-
305-and one can provide trivial answers that aren't mathematically interesting,
306-e.g. the set `{n : ℕ | P n}` itself. The question of whether the answer
307-provided corresponds to a mathematically meaningful solution of the problem
308-is outside of the scope of this repository.

310-## Style guidelines
311-
312-- One problem per file (variants and special cases may share a file).
313-- Include a reference comment linking to the source of the conjecture.
314-- Use `theorem` or `lemma` for problem statements.
315-- Bespoke definitions are allowed when they help clarify problem statements;
316-  add basic API tests for them.
317-- Do not introduce placeholder definitions (e.g. `def foo : Type := sorry` or
318-  `opaque foo : Type*`), incomplete type annotations, holes, or new axioms. All
319-  referenced definitions must exist, and all imports must be correct.
320-- Every statement should have at least one `AMS` subject tag.
321-- Every file should be put in the corresponding directory of the repository,
322-  e.g. a problem sourced from Wikipedia should live in
323-  `FormalConjectures/Wikipedia`.
324-- When a problem is stated as a question in English, the preferred style is
325:  to use `answer(sorry)`:
326-
327-  ```lean
328-  /-- English version: "Does P hold?" -/
329:  theorem myConjecture : answer(sorry) ↔ P := by
330-    sorry
331-  ```
332-
333-  This way the informal "Does ...", "Are there ..." or "Is it true that ..."
334:  corresponds to the `answer(sorry)` in the formalised statement. If the
335:  problem has been solved, `answer(sorry)` should be replaced by
336:  `answer(True)` or `answer(False)` accordingly.
337-
338-  If the problem is not stated as a question, the following style is preferred:
339-
340-  ```lean
341-  /-- English version: "P holds" -/
342-  theorem myConjecture : P := by
343-    sorry
344-  ```
345-
346-  If the problem has been solved to the negative, then `P` should be replaced
347-  with `¬ P`.
348-- Follow the same AI usage conventions as
349-  [Mathlib](https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/index.html).
350-- Use tex for math in comments, e.g. `If $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ has $\sum_{n \in A}\frac 1 n = \infty$`
351-

353-
354-All submissions, including submissions by project members, require review. We
355-use GitHub pull requests for this purpose. Consult
356-[GitHub Help](https://help.github.com/articles/about-pull-requests/) for more
357-information on using pull requests.

359-## Managing labels
360-
361-Any user can add or remove certain labels on pull requests and issues by
362-leaving a comment. The supported labels are: `awaiting-author`, `WIP`, `Easy`,
363-and `documentation`.
364-
365-- **To add a label**: Leave a comment with `+` followed by the exact label
366-  name on a line by itself. For compatibility, the exact label name without
367-  `+` also works. For example:
368-  ```text
369-  +awaiting-author
370-  ```
371-- **To remove a label**: Leave a comment with `-` followed by the exact label
372-  name on a line by itself. For example:
373-  ```text
374-  -awaiting-author
375-  ```
